¶ 39. Hours] Recalling the horae of Greek myth, goddesses of the hours and seasons.
 the open sky] the sky Mary Nbk. sky,] sky; Nbk 14.
 Then . . . bare] Cp. the description of sunrise in TL 1–20; and The Cloud 77–84.
 The sunbeams . . . Deceit] Cp. Epipsychidion 163–69, on the ‘light’ of the ‘Imagination’, which ‘fills’:
The Universe with glorious beams, and kills
Error, the worm, with many a sun-like arrow
Of its reverberated lightning.
 my shafts] Arrows; Apollo’s numerous attributes included skill in archery (he lists further attain-
ments in lines 33–35). Cp. Could Arethusa to her fountain run (Longman v, no. 411Appendix K) 3–4.
 actions,] actions Nbk 14.
 Cp. The Cloud 1–4.
 clouds,] clouds Nbk 14.
 ethereal] Delicate. colours;] colours, Nbk 14.

paragraphs.source_en:
25 I stand at noon upon the peak of Heaven;
Then with unwilling steps, I?[linger] down
To the clouds of the Atlantic even.
 For grief that I depart they weep and frown —
What look is more delightful, than the smile
30 With which I soothe them from the Western isle?
